was produced by vacuum induction melting and casting in a pure argon atmosphere. Melting was carried out in a periclase crucible, starting from the melting and degassing in a vacuum of inactive charge components (iron, nickel, cobalt). Then, carbon, chromium, and manganese were sequentially introduced into the melt through a dispenser. The molten metal was casted in an argon atmosphere into a flat mold.
three other portions were subjected to different thermal treatments: (L-SST, long solid solution treatment) 300-min annealing at T = 1200 °C, water-quenching
(Ms-HQ, multistage heating/quenching) ten cycles of heating to T = 1200 °C with subsequent quenching without exposure at high temperature

attributes.size: transverse size about 3 ± 1 μm, longitudinal size up to tens of micrometers
attributes.composition: Cr and C enriched, Co, Fe, Ni depleted

evidence.quote: EBSD phase analysis gives a M7C3 phase as the most probable one (the mean CI is 0.47), but the identification of the same particles with M23C6 phase is also possible with lower CI. That is, some carbides type M7C3 and M23C6 could be confused in the EBSD phase analysis

Both solid-solution-based treatments, L-SST and Ms-SST, cause a sufficient growth of the aγ-value: up to 3.615 ± 0.002 Å and 3.616 ± 0.003 Å, respectively

attributes.morphology: more spherical relative to the cast state

evidence.quote: After uninterrupted solid-solution treatment for 300-min (L-SST), the volume content of particles has slightly decreased to 10.0 ± 0.5% without pronounced changing in their size. Partial dissolution of the precipitates provides their "smoothing", carbides look more spherical relative to the cast state
the Ms-HQ treatment does not change a lattice parameter of austenitic phase relative to the cast material (aγ = 3.611 ± 0.002 Å)

attributes.size: partial fragmentation, small particles about 1 μm form

evidence.quote: Ten heating/quenching cycles (Ms-HQ) in the temperature range (RT-1200 °C) lead to insufficient decrease in the volume content of carbide phase (11.0 ± 0.5%) and weak smoothing of the particles. But the spreading of the interphase boundaries arises due to the partial fragmentation of carbides
Both solid-solution-based treatments, L-SST and Ms-SST, cause a sufficient growth of the aγ-value: up to 3.615 ± 0.002 Å and 3.616 ± 0.003 Å, respectively
After Ms-SST, the volume content of carbide phase is the smallest among all treatment regimes (9.5 ± 0.5%), and the transverse size of the particles decreases down to 2.0 ± 0.5 μm
